notes: Cold SQLite after approved reboot; not a matched warm comparison.
Two actual scheduler jobs observed; eventual ready/handoff 162669 ms; attachment-to-ready gap 152931 ms.

limits: Includes SSH transport and terminal output delivery, not physical presentation or CPU time.
Retained initialized session, not startup latency.

conclusions: The fixed one-worker image executed its handoff paint at 51986 ms, but the 38584 ms attachment-to-ready gap remained.
The attempted two-worker fixed-image trial blocked before placement/runtime initialization and is not a valid worker comparison.
At its stop request the latter VM had one pending synchronous filesystem request and no native jobs.
HTTP file access first timed out and then refused connections, while SSH remained available.
Both temporary dotenv files were removed and verified absent; the second required an approved rig reboot to restore filesystem access.

The recovered valid two-worker run eventually painted ready and handoff at 162669 ms, 152931 ms after attachment. A completed continuation maximum reached 126018 ms. Once settled, five draft echo samples had median 29.640 ms / max 30.547 ms.
followup_diagnostics_status: Additional guard/event/drain/render probes passed exact TRUEOS check; current source keeps one worker by default and a startup-only optional-prewarm defer experiment is being added. Pre-Rustc pack was intentionally terminated before these source changes; final package rebuild pending.
limits: One fixed one-worker run and an invalid two-worker attempt do not establish a performance regression or speedup.
SQLite was warm; application timings begin after loading and do not measure full download-to-ready startup.
Host loader probes were absent and Hull/native PID identity cannot be uniquely joined by PID.
Continuation ages, ABI snapshots and candidate counts are not CPU attribution.
